sections.section_name: Electrical (As Specifically Listed - NONE Listed - Flag)
sections.notes: Zero electrical confirmed by answer — no rough-in, no devices; the 6h/$95 carry has no component and should size to zero (would otherwise be rough_meps, never an interior component)

flags.message: Footprint is settled by answer at the drawing's 22'-11" × 11'-8" clear (267 sqft), so every proposal/JBD quantity still carrying 294 sqft (slab, excavation, roof area, rafters, gutter removal, perimeter) runs ~9% high; only the paver demo area stays at 294 because it measures the existing field, not the new slab.

Knee wall is settled at ~3'-4" with prefinished white vinyl lap siding outside and prefinished beadboard inside, but the JBD prices a 2' wall over 60 LF with a single $345 'white vinyl finish' line and no beadboard — the wall is 67% taller (~107 sqft per face, ~214 sqft of cladding) on ~32 LF, so its 48h/$1,713 section is wrong in both directions and its hours are coincidental, not derived.

Painting is confirmed out of scope (siding/beadboard prefinished, rafters/trim as delivered, brick unpainted) — the drawings' white-painted rafters and p5 'brick painted to match house' note are visualization-only; sizing must carry zero paint hours and the customer walkthrough should expect unpainted rafters.

The veneer-coverage answer puts customer-selected veneer on the exterior chase faces, while drawing p5 shows those faces as brick and the paint answer refers to 'chimney brick' — whether the exterior is the $5/sf stone veneer or a separate brick veneer is unstated; area (~150 sqft) is the same either way, but brick veneer would be a different crew/rate and a separate material not in any allowance.

Post count is settled at 7-9 (carried 8) but the JBD prices 5 posts and zero turned-down footings — post material, footing forming, and ~0.5-0.7 cy extra concrete are missing from its concrete and framing sections, so its 42h/70h should not be read as covering them; the smaller slab happens to offset the missing footing volume so the 4.2 cy ready-mix lands roughly right.

JBD carries $0 permits and no inspection lines while answers confirm a Johnson City building permit with three visits — footing (before the pour), framing, and fireplace/chimney; permit_items and bundled_inspections receive essentially no JBD hours but must not be zero downstream (canon 2h per visit ≈ 6h), and the footing inspection is a hard gate between forms/rebar and the pour that the JBD's 42h concrete line assumes away.

JBD roof-structure labor includes 'chimney-penetration framing', TL 8h for 10-3-2 chimney-height work, and $245 roof flashing/storm collar, but the settled location and termination put the chimney outside the shed roof edge ending just above the low eave — that work reduces to a chase-to-eave counterflash detail, not a penetration or tall chase.

The chimney-termination policy (cap just above the ~8' low eave, not above the shed roof's high side) sits below the roof plane within 10' horizontally, which is the geometry 10-3-2 normally forbids — the confirmed fireplace/chimney inspection is where this could be rejected, so sizing should not treat the chase height as final until the inspector or the firebox manufacturer's termination table signs off.

Gutter answer end-caps the existing run at the tie-in and leaves the downspout in place, but no source says which side of the ~23' removed section the downspout sits on — if it was on the removed run, the capped upstream gutter has no outlet and an unpriced downspout is coming; if outside, it is a single trivial end-cap.

Roof structure 70h for a ~290 sqft single-plane shed with ~18 rafters, two beams, ~8 posts and 10 sheets runs hot; rate card gives ~8 posts × 0.75 + 2 beams × ~7 + 18 rafters × 0.5 + 10 sheets × 0.4 ≈ 33h plus tie-in and layout, i.e. a 3-person crew in 2-2.5 days (~50h) — the eave tie-in is gutter removal plus one end-cap, not eave surgery.

Fireplace structure 98h (90h GL) is heavy now that a manufactured firebox + Class A pipe in a ~6'-wide framed chase terminating at the low eave is settled and all veneer has moved to the finish section — rate card gives chase 12 + firebox 4-6 + pipe 6-8 + counterflash 2-4 + cement board substrate ≈ 26-34h for a 2-person crew; the 98h only made sense against the masonry option now off the table.

Fireplace finish 40h is roughly in line now that veneer covers ~150 sqft (interior face + exterior chase faces): rate card lath/scratch 150 × 0.06 = 9 + veneer 150 × 0.17 = 26 + hearth 24 × 0.25 = 6 + mantel 2-3 ≈ 44h — the JBD's 150 SF was a planning number that happens to match the settled coverage, so this section should not be trimmed as hot.

Screened enclosure 48h is built on the wrong wall (60 LF × 2' vinyl); the governing ~32 LF × 3'-4" wall with vinyl lap siding, beadboard, screen frames, ~25 sqft of small frieze/transom bays, one door and trim — rate card gives kneewall 32 × 0.25 + screen frames 35 × 0.35 + siding 107 × 0.08 + beadboard 107 × 0.08 + trim/cap + door 4h ≈ 40h, plus choppy frieze-bay screening the JBD never priced — net effort is comparable but not derived.
Electrical 6h and $95 material carried for a scope confirmed zero-electrical with no rough-in — this collapses to 0h; the JBD's own PM notes anticipated this.

General conditions 30h includes 18h PM for fireplace-system and finish-selection coordination that is now complete per answers (all selections final, lead times known) — remaining PM effort is scheduling, permit pull, and three inspection calls, closer to 8-12h; the 4h GL staging/protection is in line with canon (4-6h staging + 2h protection).

Demolition 20h vs rate card ~294 sqft × 0.02 = 6h pavers + 4h fire pit + 1.5h sawcut ≈ 11.5h for a 3-person machine-assisted crew — the JBD runs ~75% hot even allowing for 'heavy' loading; the 3-crew mobilization floor and dumpster loading, not the arithmetic, justify anything above ~12h.

No roof pitch or beam/post sizing exists in any source (to be sized in-house per IRC tables, not yet done); roof area is carried as plan area (~290 sqft) with no slope factor, the frieze/transom band height is undimensioned, and the chase/cap height is unknown even though termination is settled at 'just above the low eave' — sizing tolerates this (low-slope shed, ±5%) so these are null/low quantities, not blocking questions.

Firebox + Class A kit lead time is 3-4 weeks and the kit dimensions drive the fireplace footing thickening that the footing inspector will look at before the pour — under 'no demo without materials' the kit (or at least its spec sheet) must be in hand before forms are set, which the JBD's ~5-6 wk duration does not account for; with a 2027-03-01 start the order must be placed by early February 2027.

Concrete patio is mapped to groundwork (foundation before framing) rather than concrete_landscape because it carries the fireplace footing, every post footing, and the pre-pour footing inspection; downstream should expect no separate flatwork phase after the shell, and yard restoration is excluded by the JBD.

Screened enclosure splits three ways with real work in each: framing (knee wall + screen frames + frieze bays) → structural_framing, exterior vinyl lap siding + trim → cladding_roof, interior beadboard + screening + door → interior_installs; the JBD's single 48h line cannot be apportioned from its own text, so any split is a judgment.

General conditions is shared between procurement_items and permit_items because the confirmed permit pull and three inspection calls are PM work with no JBD line of their own; the JBD's own header says 'No Permits', so the permit_items share is inferred from the answers, not the estimate.

Fireplace structure and finish land on their dedicated components; the finish component's Exterior Finishes home is now a partial fit since the exterior chase faces are veneered there, but the interior face, hearth, and mantel are inside the screened porch and must follow the chimney inspection — downstream should not sequence it ahead of the chase inspection just because of the phase label.

Interior trade concurrency (max two trades inside) applies to the screened porch once the roof is on: beadboard/screening, fireplace veneer, and screen door hang are all 'inside' — downstream should not stack more than two of them.
